kid.simple: A TextButton is a box with text that players can click or tap. It looks like a TextLabel but also has button events like Activated. Use it for Play, Buy, Close, and any other clickable word.
kid.analogy: A TextButton is like an elevator button with a label on it: it shows words like 'Lobby' and does something when you press it.
whenToUse: Play, Settings, Close, Buy buttons
Menu tabs
Any clickable text
kid.where: Inside a ScreenGui (or a SurfaceGui/BillboardGui that's in PlayerGui). The click code must be in a LocalScript, often placed right inside the button in StarterGui.

terms.UI / GUI: User Interface: the buttons, menus, text and pictures drawn on the screen or on things in the game.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. All UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.ScreenGui: The invisible container that holds UI shown on the player's screen. It must be inside the player's PlayerGui (put it in StarterGui in Studio).
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside.
terms.UDim2: The value used for Size and Position: (X Scale, X Offset, Y Scale, Y Offset). Scale is a fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size; Offset is exact pixels.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.transparency: How see-through something is. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible.
terms.Color3: A color made of red, green and blue amounts, like Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0) for red.
terms.font: The style of the letters, like Arial, Comic, or a blocky game font.
terms.rich text: Text with simple tags inside it, like word, that make parts bold, italic or colored.
terms.grapheme: One visible character, like a letter, a number, or a symbol.
terms.wrap: When text reaches the edge, it continues on the next line.
terms.truncate: Cut off text that's too long, often adding '...' at the end.
terms.read-only: You can read the value but not change it.
terms.localization: Translating text into the player's language.
terms.deprecated: Old and replaced by something better. Don't use it in new code.
terms.Activated: The button's main 'pressed' event. Works with mouse, touch and gamepad.
terms.RemoteEvent: A messenger that lets a LocalScript tell the server something happened, like 'I clicked Buy'.
terms.server: Roblox's computer that runs the game for everyone. Important things like giving coins must happen there.

examples.title: A button that opens and closes a menu
examples.place: LocalScript inside a TextButton, in a ScreenGui in StarterGui that also has a Frame named "Menu"
examples.code:
local button = script.Parent
local menu = button.Parent:WaitForChild("Menu")

menu.Visible = false
button.Text = "Open Menu"

button.Activated:Connect(function()
	menu.Visible = not menu.Visible -- flip between shown and hidden
	if menu.Visible then
		button.Text = "Close Menu"
	else
		button.Text = "Open Menu"
	end
end)
explain: button.Parent is the ScreenGui, where we find the Menu frame.
Activated fires on click, tap, or gamepad A press.
'not menu.Visible' flips true to false and false to true, so each press toggles the menu.
We also change the button's text so players know what it will do next.

gotchas: Click code must run in a LocalScript. To change coins or give items, send a RemoteEvent to the server.
Use Activated, not MouseButton1Click, so phone and console players can press it too.
Want a plain rectangle button without words? Set TextTransparency to 1 or leave Text empty.

class/TextChannel.d:
Represents a text chat channel. Contains TextSources as descendants.

To send a chat message to the TextChannel, call TextChannel:SendAsync() from a LocalScript. The corresponding TextSource of the user with TextSource.CanSend = true must be in that channel.

Messages from different TextChannels can be separated into different tabs in the chat window using ChannelTabsConfiguration. Multiple channels with the same name might cause unexpected behavior with the chat window, even if the player isn't a member of the other channels.

To learn more, see In-Experience Text Chat.

m.d: The TextChannel will only deliver messages to users that can send direct messages to the DirectChatRequester. This property can only be set using SetDirectChatRequester().
m.s: The `TextChannel` will only deliver messages to users that can send direct messages to the `DirectChatRequester`.

m.d:
Adds a TextSource to the TextChannel given userId of the user (with Player.UserId). Can only be used in a Script.

If a TextSource representing the user does not exist, this adds a TextSource.

If a TextSource representing the user does exist, this returns the TextSource.

If the user has chat off or isn't in the server, this returns a tuple nil, false.
m.s: Adds a `Class.TextSource` to the `Class.TextChannel` given userId of a `Class.Player`.

p.s: The userId of the Player.

r.s: Returns TextSource and true if a new TextSource is created for the user, TextSource and false if there is an existing TextSource, or nil and false if the user has chat off or is not in this server.

m.d: Displays a system message to user. Can only be used in a LocalScript, or in a Script with RunContext of RunContext.Client. Messages are only visible to that user and aren't automatically filtered or localized.
m.s: Displays a system message to the user.

p.s: The system message sent to the TextChannel.
Use to identify system message types, such as the default system messages.

r.s: A TextChatMessage with TextChatMessage.Status property that indicates the condition of the message.

m.d:
Sends a TextChatMessage to the server. Can only be used in a LocalScript, or in a Script with RunContext of RunContext.Client. Please note that only messages typed and sent by the user will be delivered.

The metadata argument has a limit of 200 characters. If this is called with a metadata argument that has more than 200 characters, the message will not be sent to other users. Instead, the sender will receive a TextChatMessage with the TextChatMessage.Metadata and TextChatMessage.Text properties set to empty strings.
m.s: Sends a `Class.TextChatMessage` to the server.

p.s: The message to send to the TextChannel.
Custom metadata to attach to the message.

r.s: A TextChatMessage with TextChatMessage.Status property that indicates the condition of the message.

m.d:
Sets the DirectChatRequester for the TextChannel. This method is only available for use in server scripts.

Use this API if you are working with TextChatService and have a custom implementation of direct chat outside of the default text channels.

When called on a TextChannel that is parented to TextChatService and has no existing TextSources, SetDirectChatRequester adds the requested users as a TextSource and set the DirectChatRequester property for the channel.

When DirectChatRequester is set, only messages between users that can direct chat with the DirectChatRequester are delivered.
m.s: Sets the `Class.TextChannel.DirectChatRequester|DirectChatRequester` for the `TextChannel`. The `TextChannel` will only deliver messages to users that can send direct messages to the `DirectChatRequester`.

p.s: The Player whose direct-message permissions gate the channel; only users who can send direct messages to this player are delivered messages on the channel.

m.d:
Like TextChatService.MessageReceived, fires when TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage() is invoked on the client, or when the client receives a valid TextChannel:SendAsync() response from the server. This event is only fired on the client.

If the server's TextChannel.ShouldDeliverCallback property is bound and returns false, the client will not fire TextChannel.MessageReceived.

Use the TextChatMessage parameter to get the TextSource and the text of the message (with TextChatMessage.Text).

The TextChatMessage parameter is the final result of any functions bound to TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage or TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage.
m.s: Fires when `Class.TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage()` is invoked on the client, or when the client receives a valid `Class.TextChannel:SendAsync()` response from the server.

p.s: The received TextChatMessage.

m.d:
Called when TextChannel is receiving an incoming message. Can only be implemented on the client.

Use this to decorate TextChatMessages. If this callback returns a TextChatMessageProperties, those properties are merged with the TextChatMessage parameter to create a new TextChatMessage.

When bound to the client sending a message, this callback is run twice; first when the message is initially sent and received locally, and again when the client receives the result of the filtered message from the server.

TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage callbacks always run after the TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage callback.

This should be defined only once per TextChannel in the source code. Multiple bindings to the same channel will override one another in a nondeterministic manner.

When TextChatService:CreateDefaultTextChannels() is true, those default TextChannels have their TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage callbacks assigned internally in order to exhibit special default behavior.
m.s: Called when `Class.TextChannel` is receiving an incoming message.

p.s: The incoming TextChatMessage.

r.s: If a TextChatMessageProperties is returned, those properties are merged with the TextChatMessage parameter to create a new TextChatMessage with those properties.

m.d:
Called for each client when TextChannel is receiving an incoming message to determine whether or not it should be delivered to that client. Can only be defined on the server.

Once defined, this callback needs to return a truthy value such as true, 1, or "hello" to deliver the message to said client. If the callback returns anything else (including nil), the message won't be delivered to that client, although the sender will see the message regardless.

The sender can be referenced by TextChatMessage.TextSource, while the receiver is the textSource argument. Note that the sender and receiver can be the same, as the callback iterates through all possible receivers.
m.s: Called for each client when `Class.TextChannel` is receiving an incoming message to determine whether or not it should be delivered to that client.

p.s: The message being sent, which also contains the sender of the message.
The TextSource of the user who will be receiving the message.

r.s: A truthy value (such as true, 1, or a non-empty string) to deliver the message to the given client, or a falsy value (including nil) to withhold it from that client.

class/TextChannelWindow.d:
TextChannelWindow is a GuiObject that renders in-experience text chat messages from a linked TextChannel. Place it under a ScreenGui or other LayerCollector descendant to display chat in a custom location and layout.

Set Target to a TextChannel to choose which channel's messages the window shows. The window registers itself with TextChatService when added to the data model.

Properties set on ChatWindowConfiguration do not apply to this window.

Accepted children: UICorner, UIAspectRatioConstraint, UISizeConstraint, and scripts (LocalScript, Script, ModuleScript); other child types are rejected.

m.d:
A reference to the TextChannel whose messages this window renders. When set, the window shows messages from the specified channel. Setting this property to nil disconnects the window from any channel so it displays no messages.

The default value is nil (no channel linked).
Font used to render this window's messages and its input bar. Applied only when TextChannelWindow.UseDefaultFont is false.
m.s: Font used to render text in this window.

m.d: When true (default), the window uses the live platform default font. When false, the window uses FontFace.
m.s: Whether this window uses the live platform default font.

class/TextChatCommand.d:
Represents a text chat command. Can be used to create custom text chat commands when parented to TextChatService.

Custom commands can have up to two aliases, and the Triggered event fires when a user's message matches the value of either the PrimaryAlias or SecondaryAlias. For an example of custom commands, see Custom text chat commands.

To learn more about using TextChatService, see In-experience text chat.

m.d:
Whether this TextChatCommand appears as a suggestion in the chat autocomplete menu. Defaults to true.

When true, PrimaryAlias is offered in the autocomplete list. Set to false to hide it from suggestions; the command still works when typed in full via PrimaryAlias or SecondaryAlias.

Autocomplete itself is controlled by ChatInputBarConfiguration.AutocompleteEnabled.
m.s: Determines whether the `Class.TextChatCommand` is shown as a suggestion in the chat autocomplete menu.

m.d:
Determines whether the TextChatCommand is enabled.

When disabled, messages that match the value of PrimaryAlias or SecondaryAlias are not sunk and is sent to other users.

Use this to disable default commands on a case-by-case basis.
m.s: Determines whether the `Class.TextChatCommand` is enabled.

m.d:
A primary alias used to trigger the TextChatCommand.

If a user sends a message with TextChannel:SendAsync() that matches the PrimaryAlias, the message is not sent and instead TextChatCommand.Triggered is fired.
m.s: A primary alias used to trigger the `Class.TextChatCommand`.

m.d:
A secondary alias used to trigger the TextChatCommand, in addition to its PrimaryAlias.

If a user sends a message with TextChannel:SendAsync() that matches the SecondaryAlias, the message is not sent and instead TextChatCommand.Triggered is fired, exactly as it is for the PrimaryAlias. Matching is case-insensitive, and the alias must be followed by the end of the message or a space, so a SecondaryAlias of "/e" matches "/e" and "/e dance" but not "/emote".

Defaults to an empty string, in which case only the PrimaryAlias triggers the command.
m.s: A secondary alias used to trigger the `Class.TextChatCommand`.

m.d:
An event that developers can bind to execute commands.

When a user sends a message to the server via TextChannel:SendAsync(), the message is intercepted by the TextChatCommand and not replicated to other users if the content of the message matches the PrimaryAlias or SecondaryAlias.

For example, for a TextChatCommand with TextChatCommand.PrimaryAlias as "mute", if a user sends "/mute SomeUserName", then the relevant TextChatCommand for mute will fire its TextChatCommand.Triggered. The message "/mute SomeUserName" is not replicated to other users.
m.s: An event that developers can bind to execute commands.

p.s: A reference to the TextSource responsible for triggering the command via TextChannel:SendAsync().
The full, unfiltered text used to trigger the command that can be used to dissect parameters from the command message.

A reference to the BubbleChatMessageProperties instance that overrides BubbleChatConfiguration properties for this individual message's chat bubble.

This property is nil by default. This property is nil by default. It is populated when your TextChatService.OnChatWindowAdded callback returns a ChatWindowMessageProperties instance, typically created with ChatWindowConfiguration:DeriveNewMessageProperties(): the returned instance is stored here on the resulting TextChatMessage. Any properties set on it take precedence over the shared ChatWindowConfiguration when the message is rendered.
m.s: A reference to the `Class.ChatWindowMessageProperties` that overrides the appearance of this message in the chat window.

m.d: A unique identifier for the TextChatMessage.
m.s: A unique identifier for the `Class.TextChatMessage`.

m.d:
A general purpose field for storing miscellaneous data about the TextChatMessage. The second argument of TextChannel:SendAsync() and TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage() is used to populate this field.

Use this field to apply additional formatting for special messages within TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage and TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage callbacks.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")

local customChannel: TextChannel = Instance.new("TextChannel")
customChannel.Parent = TextChatService:WaitForChild("TextChannels")

customChannel.OnIncomingMessage = function(message: TextChatMessage)
  if string.find(message.Metadata, "Error") then
    local overrideProperties = Instance.new("TextChatMessageProperties")
    overrideProperties.Text = string.format("<font color='rgb(255,0,0)'>%s</font>", message.Text)
    return overrideProperties
  elseif string.find(message.Metadata, "Info") then
    local overrideProperties = Instance.new("TextChatMessageProperties")
    overrideProperties.Text = string.format("<font color='rgb(0, 255, 150)'>%s</font>", message.Text)
    return overrideProperties
  end

  return nil
end

Players.LocalPlayer.CharacterAdded:Connect(function()
  customChannel:DisplaySystemMessage("This is an error!", "Game.Error.Generic")
  customChannel:DisplaySystemMessage("Could not find save data!", "Game.Error.SaveDataNotFound")

  customChannel:DisplaySystemMessage("You won the game!", "Game.Info.Win")
  customChannel:DisplaySystemMessage("You lost the game!", "Game.Info.Lose")
end)

class/TextChatMessageProperties.d:
Overrides TextChatMessage properties like ChatWindowMessageProperties and BubbleChatMessageProperties when returned by callbacks defined in TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage or TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage. These properties are useful for customizing the appearance of a message with rich text tags.

For sample code, see Assign chat tags.

If you return empty strings for any of these properties, TextChatService ignores them and doesn't override the original values.

class/TextChatService.d:
A service handling in-experience text chat, including managing TextChannels, decorating messages, filtering text, creating TextChatCommands, and developing custom chats interfaces. To learn more, see text chat overview.

For further customization, TextChatService has the following singleton children:

  • ChatWindowConfiguration
  • ChatInputBarConfiguration
  • BubbleChatConfiguration
  • ChannelTabsConfiguration

To display content from a TextChannel in a custom location, place a TextChannelWindow under a ScreenGui or SurfaceGui.
class/TextChatService.s: A service handling in-experience text chat.

m.d: Determines whether a user has chat translation enabled. If true, messages the user receives will be translated into their preferred language. Use TextChatMessage.Translation to get the message translation. This property is client-side only and reflects the user's own preference; read it from a LocalScript to adapt custom chat UIs when the user toggles translation.
m.s: Determines whether a user has chat translation enabled.

m.d: Determines whether to fully enable TextChatService or revert to the legacy chat system. Setting this property to ChatVersion.LegacyChatService effectively disables TextChatService.
m.s: Determines whether to fully enable `Class.TextChatService` or revert to the legacy chat system.
m.dep: This property has been deprecated in newly created Studio experiences. TextChatService is the only allowed chat system and is automatically enabled.

m.d:
Determines whether TextChatService should create default TextChatCommands. If true, the following TextChatCommands are created and put in a Folder named TextChatCommands inside TextChatService:

Name Primary Alias Secondary Alias Description Usage Example
RBXClearCommand clear cls Clears the chat log for the local user. /cls
RBXConsoleCommand console Opens the Developer Console. /console
RBXEmoteCommand emote e Plays an avatar emote. /e dance
RBXHelpCommand help ? Shows a list of chat commands. /help
RBXMuteCommand mute m Mutes a user by their Class.Player.Name|Name or Class.Player.DisplayName|DisplayName in all Class.TextChannel|TextChannels. /m Username
RBXTeamCommand team t Enters team chat mode where messages are only visible to teammates. /t
RBXUnmuteCommand unmute um Unmutes a user by their Class.Player.Name|Name or Class.Player.DisplayName|DisplayName in all Class.TextChannel|TextChannels. /um Username
RBXVersionCommand version v Shows the chat version. /version
RBXWhisperCommand whisper w Enters whisper mode with another Class.Player. /w DisplayName or /w @Username

Note that you can edit, create, and remove TextChatCommands even if CreateDefaultCommands is true. Also note that mute and unmute commands apply to all TextChannels.
m.s: Determines whether `Class.TextChatService` should create default `Class.TextChatCommand|TextChatCommands`.

m.d:
Determines whether TextChatService should create default TextChannels. If true, a Folder named TextChannels is created inside TextChatService at runtime to contain the TextChannels outlined in the table below. Each of the default channels has the described special behavior applied to messages using its internally bound TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage callback function, changing how messages appear when sent through the channel. The callback is assigned automatically either at runtime (if the TextChannel exists) or when the TextChannel is created.

Channel Description
RBXGeneral Class.TextChannel for player messages. In the chat window, messages are modified such that Class.TextChatMessage.PrefixText|PrefixText receives a rich text font color tag to give chatting players their distinctive name color. If Class.Player.Team exists, that Class.Team.TeamColor is used instead of the default name color.
RBXSystem Class.TextChannel for system messages. In the chat window, messages are modified such that Class.TextChatMessage.Text is given a light grey color tag by default, or a red color tag if Class.TextChatMessage.Metadata contains the word "Error".
RBXTeam[BrickColor] Class.TextChannel for team-specific player messages, created when a Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor is in use by any Class.Team within the Class.Teams service. Name of the created channel is RBXTeam followed by the Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor name. For example, RBXTeamCrimson is a Class.TextChannel created when there is an active team whose Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor property is the "Crimson" Datatype.BrickColor.

In the chat window, messages are modified such that Class.TextChatMessage.PrefixText|PrefixText is colored according to the Class.Player.TeamColor|TeamColor and is prepended with [Team].

Team channels create Class.TextSource|TextSources for all non‑Class.Player.Neutral|Neutral players with the matching Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor, allowing them to use team‑only chat. Channels are removed if there are no remaining teams with an associated Class.Team.TeamColor|TeamColor.
RBXWhisper:[UserId1]_[UserId2] Class.TextChannel for whisper messages between two players, created when a player uses the /whisper command on another player. For example RBXWhisper:2276836_505306092 is a Class.TextChannel for players with Class.Player.UserId|UserIds 2276836 and 505306092. Inside whisper channels are two Class.TextSource|TextSources associated with the respective Class.Player.UserId|UserIds.

In the chat window, messages are colored the same as those in RBXGeneral and Class.TextChatMessage.PrefixText is modified to show whether a message was sent from or received by the local user.

Whisper channels are removed when either player leaves the experience.

Note that the default TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage callbacks can be overwritten. Also note that you can edit, create, and remove TextChannels even if CreateDefaultTextChannels is true.

Messages from different TextChannels can be separated into different tabs in the chat window using ChannelTabsConfiguration.
m.s: Determines whether `Class.TextChatService` should create default `Class.TextChannel|TextChannels`.

m.d: Requires RobloxScript security; not accessible from experience scripts. Controls whether platform-integrated chat is enabled for the experience. When set to RolloutState.Enabled, TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage and TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage callbacks from developer scripts are not invoked, and only CoreScripts can set those callbacks. When set to RolloutState.Disabled, behavior is explicitly disabled. Defaults to RolloutState.Default.
m.s: Determines whether platform-integrated chat is enabled for the experience. Requires `RobloxScript` security.

m.d: Determines whether a user has permission to chat in experiences. Factors such as parental control settings may prevent the user from sending messages. Errors if the userId is not in the current server. Note that this method can be used with all current player UserIds in a Script with RunContext of RunContext.Server or RunContext.Legacy. This method can also be used in a LocalScript but only with the UserId of the local player.
m.s: Determines whether a user has permission to chat in experiences.

p.s: The Player.UserId of the user whose chat permission is being checked.

r.s: A boolean indicating whether the user has permission to chat.

m.d:
Determines whether or not two users can receive messages from each other. Both users must be in the current server, otherwise an error will occur.

Factors such as incompatible parental control settings or blocked status may prevent the delivery of messages between users (TextChannels internally use this result to determine whether to deliver messages between users). Note that this method is only available for use in a Script with RunContext of RunContext.Server or RunContext.Legacy.
m.s: Determines whether or not two users can receive messages from each other.

p.s: The Player.UserId of the potential message sender.
The Player.UserId of the potential message receiver.

r.s: A boolean indicating whether the two users can exchange messages.

m.d:
Determines whether a user has permission to chat directly with other users in experiences based on their parental control settings, such as a whisper channel between two users. To be used when:

  • The line of communication is user-initiated (not developer- or gameplay-initiated).
  • Access to the communication is closed and limited.

You may use this method to gate certain features in your experience depending on the result.

When creating a TextChannel for a direct chat, use TextChannel:SetDirectChatRequester to set the requesterUserId so that the channel can determine whether to deliver messages between users. When TextChannel.DirectChatRequester is non-nil, TextChannels internally use this result to determine whether to deliver messages between users.

Note that this method is only available for use in a Script with RunContext of RunContext.Server or RunContext.Legacy.
m.s: Determines whether a user has permission to chat directly with other users in experiences based on factors such as their parental control settings.

p.s: The user who would have initiated the direct chat request. If the user is not in the current server, this method will error.
A list of users who the requesterUserId would like to chat with directly. Users not in the current server are ignored.

r.s: A list of users who could participate in the direct chat request. If none of the users can direct chat with the requesterUserId, the result is an empty array.

m.d:
Displays a chat bubble above the provided part or player character, and fires the BubbleDisplayed event with the parameters specified in this method. Can display bubbles for non-player characters (NPCs) if you specify a part within the character, such as its head.

Note that this method is only available for use in LocalScript, or in a Script with RunContext of RunContext.Client.
m.s: Displays a chat bubble above the provided part or player character.

p.s: The part or character that the bubble to be displayed above.
The text to be displayed in the chat bubble.

m.d:
Returns a sorted array of arrays of chat group IDs for the given players. Each chat group ID is a string that represents a communication-compatible group within the current universe.

If two or more players share the same chat group ID, those players are able to synchronously text chat with each other based on their age-check status and chat settings.

This method is server-side only and intended for real-time use cases such as matchmaking and teleporting. It is more efficient than calling TextChatService:CanUsersChatAsync() pairwise when evaluating many players at once, since pairwise checks scale as N^2 and cannot be merged across player lists. Chat group IDs are unique to the current universe, may change over time, and should not be stored once the user has left the experience. While you can hold onto the data returned for the purposes of gameplay while the user is in the experience, this data should not be stored after they've left.

To use this method, you must enable Chat & Voice Groups APIs in Experience Settings ⟩ Communication in Roblox Studio and agree to the Roblox Terms of Use.

In Roblox Studio this API is only available when the experience is running in Team Test.
m.s: Returns chat group IDs that indicate which players can synchronously text chat together.

p.s: A list of Players currently in the experience to evaluate for text chat compatibility.

r.s: A sorted array of arrays of chat group ID strings. Players who share a matching chat group ID are eligible to synchronously text chat with each other.

m.d: Fires when TextChatService:DisplayBubble() is called.
m.s: Fires when `Class.TextChatService:DisplayBubble()` is called.

p.s: The part or character that the bubble chat is displayed above.
The TextChatMessage associated with the bubble.

m.d:
Like TextChannel.MessageReceived, fires when TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage() is invoked on the client, or when the client receives a valid TextChannel:SendAsync() response from the server. This event is only fired on the client.

If the server's TextChannel.ShouldDeliverCallback property is bound and returns false, the client will not fire TextChatService.MessageReceived.

Use the TextChatMessage parameter to get the TextSource and the text of the message (with TextChatMessage.Text).

The TextChatMessage parameter is the final result of any functions bound to TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage or TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage.
m.s: Fires when `Class.TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage()` is invoked on the client, or when the client receives a valid `Class.TextChannel:SendAsync()` response from the server.

p.s: The received TextChatMessage.

m.d: Fires when TextChannel:SendAsync() is called by the sending client. Use this to allow placeholder messages to be shown to the user while waiting for server response to TextChannel:SendAsync().
m.s: Fires when `Class.TextChannel:SendAsync()` is called by the sending client.

p.s: The TextChatMessage from the TextChannel:SendAsync() call.

m.d:
Called when a bubble chat is about to be displayed. This can only be implemented on the client.

Use this to customize individual bubble chat messages. If this callback returns a BubbleChatMessageProperties, those properties will be applied to the associated bubble, overriding BubbleChatConfiguration properties. If a UICorner, UIGradient, or ImageLabel is parented under BubbleChatMessageProperties, they will also override their respective counterparts defined in BubbleChatConfiguration.

If the chat message is sent by a player, message.TextSource will correspond to that player, and adornee will be nil.

If the chat message is sent via TextChatService:DisplayBubble, adornee will be the partOrCharacter provided, and message.TextSource will be nil.

When bound to the client sending a message, this callback is run twice: first when the message is initially sent and received locally, then again when the client receives the result of the filtered message from the server.
m.s: Called when a bubble chat is about to be displayed.

p.s: The incoming TextChatMessage.
The part or character the bubble chat message is attached to.

r.s: If a BubbleChatMessageProperties is returned, its properties override the BubbleChatConfiguration properties.

m.d:
Called when a new message is about to be displayed in the chat window. This can only be implemented on the client.

Use this to customize individual messages that appear in the chat window. If this callback returns a ChatWindowMessageProperties, those properties will be applied to the associated message, overriding ChatWindowConfiguration properties. If a UIGradient is parented under ChatWindowMessageProperties, it will also override the TextColor3 property defined in ChatWindowConfiguration.

When bound to the client sending a message, this callback is run twice: first when the message is initially sent and received locally, then again when the client receives the result of the filtered message from the server.
m.s: Called when a new message is about to be displayed in the chat window. This can only be implemented on the client.

p.s: The incoming TextChatMessage.

r.s: If a ChatWindowMessageProperties is returned, its properties override the ChatWindowConfiguration properties.

m.d:
Called when TextChatService is receiving an incoming message. Can only be implemented on the client.

Use this to decorate TextChatMessages. If this callback returns a TextChatMessageProperties, those properties are merged with the TextChatMessage parameter to create a new TextChatMessage.

When bound to the client sending a message, this callback is run twice; first when the message is initially sent and received locally, and again when the client receives the result of the filtered message from the server.

Note that this TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage callback runs before any TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage callbacks.

This should be defined only once in the source code. Multiple bindings will override one another in a non‑deterministic manner. This callback is not invoked when TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat is set to RolloutState.Enabled.
m.s: Called when `Class.TextChatService` is receiving an incoming message.

p.s: The incoming TextChatMessage.

r.s: If a TextChatMessageProperties is returned, those properties are merged with the TextChatMessage parameter to create a new TextChatMessage with those properties, otherwise, if nil is returned, then TextChatMessage is not changed.

class/TextFilterResult.d: Represents the result of a call to TextService:FilterStringAsync(). Used to distribute a filtered string accordingly.
class/TextFilterResult.s: Represents the result of a call to `Class.TextService:FilterStringAsync()`, used to distribute a filtered string accordingly.

m.d:
This method returns the text in a properly filtered manner for the specified Player.UserId using the least restrictive filtering appropriate for that user, with Chat privacy settings of both users enforced. This should be used in the context of chats between players, although there are some other cases where text filtering is required.

The returned string should only be shown to the target user, as it might not be appropriate for all users.

If this method throws an error, the string should not be displayed to the user. Cases for error include:

  • The two users are not allowed to chat, for example if Chat:CanUserChatAsync() would return false for the given sender and receiver.
  • The user with the ID toUserId is not online on the current server.

This function will return immediately in most cases, although it will yield if the target user has just joined the server and their filtering info is not yet loaded.
m.s: Returns the text in a properly filtered manner for the specified `Class.Player.UserId`.

p.s: Player.UserId of the user being chatted.

r.s: Filtered text string.

m.dep: This method is deprecated and returns an empty string. Text filtering pertaining to chat should be done through TextChatService, and experiences that do not properly filter player-generated chat text may be subject to moderation.

m.d: Returns the text in a properly filtered manner for all users. This should be used in the context of non-chat text that every user can see, such as for a dialog that lets a user write a message on a sign, visible to all users on the server even after the author has left.
m.s: Returns the text in a properly filtered manner for all users.

r.s: Filtered text string.

m.d: Returns the text in a properly filtered manner for the specified Player.UserId based on age and other details. This should be used in the context of non-chat text that one specific user can see, such as the name of a pet.
m.s: Returns the text in a properly filtered manner for the specified `Class.Player.UserId` based on age and other details.

p.s: Player.UserId of the user intended to see/receive the text.

r.s: Filtered text string.

class/TextFilterTranslatedResult.d:
A TextFilterTranslatedResult is the object returned by TextService:FilterAndTranslateStringAsync(). It bundles the filtered source text together with filtered translations of that text into each requested target locale.

Read TextFilterTranslatedResult.SourceText and TextFilterTranslatedResult.SourceLanguage for the filtered original text and its language, call TextFilterTranslatedResult:GetTranslationForLocale() to retrieve the filtered translation for a single locale, or call TextFilterTranslatedResult:GetTranslations() to retrieve all of them at once.

Instances of this class cannot be created, parented, or replicated; they are only produced by the engine as the return value of the filtering call. That call, TextService:FilterAndTranslateStringAsync(), is deprecated, so new work should filter and translate chat through TextChatService instead.
class/TextFilterTranslatedResult.s: Holds the filtered source text and its filtered translations produced by `Class.TextService:FilterAndTranslateStringAsync()`.

m.d: The language string of the original text that was submitted to TextService:FilterAndTranslateStringAsync(). This is the source language that the translations returned by TextFilterTranslatedResult:GetTranslations() were translated from. This property is read-only.
m.s: The language of the original text that was filtered.

m.d: A TextFilterResult representing the filtered form of the original text that was submitted to TextService:FilterAndTranslateStringAsync(), in its TextFilterTranslatedResult.SourceLanguage. Use the returned TextFilterResult to obtain the correctly filtered string for each recipient before displaying the untranslated text. This property is read-only.
m.s: The filtered form of the original, untranslated text.

m.d: Returns the filtered TextFilterResult for the translation of the source text into locale, or nil if the result contains no translation for that locale. The locale argument is normalized to its language before lookup, so locale variants that share a language resolve to the same translation.
m.s: Returns the filtered translation of the source text for the given locale.

p.s: The locale identifier of the translation to retrieve.

r.s: The filtered TextFilterResult for the requested locale, or nil if the result contains no translation for it.

m.d: Returns a dictionary that maps each translation's language string to its filtered TextFilterResult. The keys are the languages that the source text was translated into for the requested target locales; use TextFilterTranslatedResult:GetTranslationForLocale() to look up a single locale directly.
m.s: Returns all filtered translations of the source text, keyed by language.

r.s: A dictionary mapping each translation's language string to its filtered TextFilterResult.

class/TextGenerator.d:
A TextGenerator instance lets you use a large language model (LLM) to generate text based on a system prompt from you and a user prompt from the player. The most common use of the API is for creating interactive non-player characters (NPCs).

For example, in a survival experience, your system prompt for a talking animal might be "You are a very busy beaver. You end all statements by mentioning how you need to get back to work on your dam.". Users could ask the beaver about water in the area, the size of a nearby forest, predators, etc.

The novelty of LLM responses can help create unique, delightful moments for players, but using the API effectively requires a bit of creativity and tuning. System prompts can be very extensive, so don't hesitate to include a long string with lots of detail.

Rate limits

Requests are initially limited to 100 per minute, which scales up based on the number of concurrent users.
class/TextGenerator.s: Gives access to a large language model for text generation.

m.d: Sets a fixed seed for the random number generator, allowing reproducible responses in cases where the same input parameters are used across multiple requests. By setting the same seed value, you can obtain identical results for debugging, testing, or evaluation purposes. The value of Seed should be an integer. Non-integral values will be truncated. Default is 0.
m.s: Sets a fixed seed for the random number generator, allowing reproducible responses in cases where the same input parameters are used across multiple requests.

m.d: Provides context to the model about its role, tone, or behavior during the conversation. This parameter can guide the model on how to respond, setting expectations like "You are an assistant" or "Use a formal tone".
m.s: Provides context to the model about its role, tone, or behavior during conversation.

m.d: Controls the "creativity" or randomness of the model's responses. Values closer to 1 increase randomness, while values closer to 0 make the responses more focused and deterministic. Values outside the accepted range are clamped to the range of [0.4, 1.0]. Default is 0.7.
m.s: Controls the "creativity" or randomness of the model's responses.

m.d: Helps the model narrow or expand the range of possible words to sample from while generating the next token. This setting narrows the token choices to only contain words that together make up a certain percentage of total likelihood (for example, 90%). A lower TopP means the model sticks to closer and more predictable choices, while a higher TopP opens the door to more diverse and creative responses. Values outside the accepted range are clamped to the range of [0.5, 1.0]. Default is 0.9.
m.s: Helps the AI model narrow or expand the range of possible words to sample from while generating the next token.

m.d:
This method returns text generated by an LLM based on the provided system and user prompts, as well as any other optional paramaters that have been set.

The request argument for this method should be a dictionary with the following structure:

Key Name Data Type Description Required
UserPrompt string Optional prompt from the user that initiates the chat. This could be a question, statement, or command that the user wants the model to respond to. No
ContextToken string Prompt history context token containing a summarization of the previous prompt requests and responses in a conversation up to the current request. If no token is provided, a new token is generated and returned in the response. Providing a previously generated context token restores the conversation state into the current request. No
MaxTokens number The maximum number of tokens in the response generated by the model. Expected to be an integer of at least 1. This limits the length of the response, preventing overly long or incomplete answers. Non-integral numbers are rounded to the nearest integer. No
JsonSchema string A JSON Schema formatted string that follows the specification at json-schema.org. When JsonSchema is provided, the model response will conform to the requested format, providing a structured output that can be parsed. No

This method returns a dictionary with the following structure:

Key Name Data Type Description
GeneratedText string The generated response.
ContextToken string A token containing the summarization of a previously passed context token and the current generated response. This token can be passed into subsequent requests to maintain the state of the current conversation. Subsequent requests generate new tokens with updated conversation state. Extracting the token and providing it maintains the ongoing conversation context.
Model string The model and version that generated the response.
m.s: Returns text generated by an LLM based on the provided system and user prompts.

p.s: A dictionary containing optional parameters for the text generation request. The currently supported parameters are UserPrompt, ContextToken, and MaxTokens.

r.s: A dictionary containing the generated response.

class/TextLabel.d:
A TextLabel renders a rectangle, like a Frame, with styled text. The rectangle can be used to define text boundaries, text scaling (TextScaled), wrapping (TextWrapped), and alignment (TextXAlignment and/or TextYAlignment).

This class contains properties that control the display of the text, such as Font and TextColor3. To display only text and hide the background rectangle, set BackgroundTransparency to 1.

A UITextSizeConstraint object can be used to constrain the size of text with TextScaled enabled. It is recommended that the size of text is no lower than 9, otherwise it may not be visible to many users.
class/TextLabel.s: A 2D user interface element that displays non-interactive text.

m.d:
This property provides a copy of Text that contains exactly what is being rendered by the TextLabel. This is useful for eliminating style tags used for rich text markup; for example, when RichText is enabled, the ContentText property shows the text as it appears to the user.

RichText Text ContentText
false <b>Hello,<br/> world!</b> <b>Hello,<br/> world!</b>
true <b>Hello,<br/> world!</b> Hello,
world!
m.s: A copy of `Class.TextLabel.Text` that contains exactly what is being rendered by the `Class.TextLabel`.

kid.simple: Read-only. The text exactly as players see it. If RichText is on, the formatting tags like are removed. For Text = "Hi" with RichText on, ContentText is "Hi".
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
print(label.ContentText)

m.d:
This property selects one of several pre-defined fonts with which the TextLabel will render its text. Some fonts have bold, italic and/or light variants.

With the exception of the Font.Legacy font, each font will render text with the line height equal to the TextSize property.

The Font.Code font is the only monospace font. It has the unique property that each character has the exact same width and height ratio of 1:2, where the width of each character is approximately half the TextSize property.

This property is kept in sync with the FontFace property.
m.s: Determines the font used to render text.

kid.simple: Picks a built-in font from a list (Enum.Font), like Gotham or Cartoon. It stays in sync with FontFace; FontFace is the newer, more flexible choice.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold

m.d:
This property is similar to the Font property but allows setting fonts that don't exist in Font.

This property is kept in sync with the Font property, such that when setting FontFace, the font is set to the corresponding Font value or to Font.Unknown if there are no matches.
m.s: Determines the font used to render text.

kid.simple: The font used to draw the text, including its weight (how bold) and style (italic). It can use fonts that aren't in the old Font list.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.FontFace = Font.new("rbxasset://fonts/families/FredokaOne.json")
-- A bold font: pass the weight when you make it
label.FontFace = Font.new("rbxasset://fonts/families/GothamSSm.json", Enum.FontWeight.Bold)

m.d: This property determines the font size to be used.
m.s: Determines the font size to be used.
m.dep: This property is deprecated in favor of TextSize which is an integer and not an enum and thus offers far more options for sizes.

kid.simple: Old — use TextSize instead.

m.d: Controls the height of lines as a multiple of the font's em square size by scaling the spacing between lines of text in the TextLabel. Valid values range from 1.0 to 3.0, defaulting to 1.0.
m.s: Scales the spacing between lines of text in the `Class.TextLabel`.

kid.simple: The space between lines of text, as a multiplier from 1 to 3. 1 is normal, 1.5 adds extra breathing room, 2 is double spacing.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.LineHeight = 1.5

m.d: This read-only property holds the automatically-localized text that the TextLabel renders. When automatic localization is enabled through AutoLocalize and the label's Text matches an entry in an applicable localization table for the player's locale, this property contains the translated string that is actually displayed; when no translation applies, it falls back to the label's own text. It defaults to an empty string and can't be set from a script.
m.s: Read-only string containing the automatically-localized text that the `Class.TextLabel` renders.

kid.simple: Read-only. The translated text actually being shown, when automatic translation (AutoLocalize) found a translation for the player's language. If no translation applies, it's just the normal text.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
print("Showing:", label.LocalizedText)

m.d:
This property controls the maximum number of graphemes (or units of text) that are shown on the TextLabel. It is primarily provided as an easy way to create a typewriter effect where the characters appear one at a time.

Changing the property does not change the position or size of the visible graphemes; the layout will be calculated as if all graphemes are visible.

Setting the property to -1 disables the limit and shows the entirety of the Text.
m.s: The maximum number of graphemes the `Class.TextLabel` can show.

kid.simple: Limits how many characters are shown. -1 (default) shows everything. Count up from 0 to make a 'typewriter' effect where letters appear one by one.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.Text = "Welcome, adventurer!"
for i = 0, #label.Text do
	label.MaxVisibleGraphemes = i
	task.wait(0.05)
end
label.MaxVisibleGraphemes = -1 -- show everything
kid.gotcha: The text layout doesn't move while letters appear; it's planned as if all the text is already there.

m.d:
This property is a comma-separated list of OpenType feature tags that are applied when the TextLabel shapes and renders its text, such as zero for slashed zeros or ss03 for a stylistic set. It defaults to an empty string, which applies no additional features.

Each entry uses the standard OpenType feature-string syntax (for example, zero or ss03). Only a supported subset of features is applied; a feature that isn't supported, a malformed string, or the bracketed partial-enabling syntax (for example, zero[1:3]) is rejected, and the reason is reported through OpenTypeFeaturesError.

This property supports styling.
m.s: Applies OpenType typographic features to the text rendered by the `Class.TextLabel`.

kid.simple: Turns on special font features using short codes separated by commas, like "zero" for a zero with a slash through it. Empty (default) means none. If a code doesn't work, OpenTypeFeaturesError says why.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.OpenTypeFeatures = "zero" -- slashed zeros, so 0 doesn't look like O

m.d:
This read-only property reports the error, if any, encountered while parsing and applying the OpenTypeFeatures string. It defaults to an empty string, which indicates that the requested features were applied successfully.

When a feature can't be applied, this property is set to one of the following messages:

  • Failed to parse features. when a feature string is malformed.
  • Unsupported feature: <tag> when a feature isn't part of the supported set.
  • Partial feature enabling not supported. when the string uses the bracketed range syntax.
m.s: Read-only property that describes why the `Class.TextLabel.OpenTypeFeatures` string could not be applied.

kid.simple: Read-only. Empty when OpenTypeFeatures worked. Otherwise a message like "Unsupported feature: xyz" telling you what went wrong.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
if label.OpenTypeFeaturesError ~= "" then
	warn(label.OpenTypeFeaturesError)
end

m.d:
This property determines whether the TextLabel renders its text using rich text markup to style sections of the string in bold, italics, specific colors, and more.

To use rich text, simply include rich text formatting tags in the Text string.
m.s: Determines whether the `Class.TextLabel` renders its text using rich text formatting.

kid.simple: When true, you can style parts of the text with tags like bold, italic or red.
kid.example: local label = script.Parent label.RichText = true label.Text = "You found a golden sword!"

m.d:
This property determines the text content rendered by the TextLabel. The visual properties of the string rendered to the screen is determined by TextColor3, TextTransparency, TextSize, Font, TextScaled, TextWrapped, TextXAlignment and TextYAlignment.

It is possible to render emoji such as 🔒 and other symbols which aren't affected by the TextColor3 property. These can be pasted into Script and LocalScript objects, as well as the field within the Properties window.

This property may contain newline characters. Similarly, this property may contain a tab character, but it will render as a space instead.
m.s: Determines the string rendered by the `Class.TextLabel`.

kid.simple: The words shown. You can use \n in a script to start a new line.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.Text = "Line one\nLine two"

m.d:
This read-only property reflects the absolute size of rendered text in offsets, meaning that if you try to fit text into a rectangle, this property would reflect the minimum dimensions of the rectangle you'd need in order to fit the text.

Using TextService:GetTextSize(), you can predict what TextBounds will be given a string, Font, TextSize, and frame size.
m.s: Read-only property which reflects the absolute size of rendered text in

kid.simple: Read-only. The size in pixels of the box the text actually needs. Handy for making a background exactly fit the text.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
print("Text needs", label.TextBounds.X, "by", label.TextBounds.Y, "pixels")

m.d: This property determines the color of text.
m.s: Determines the color of text.
m.dep: This item has been superseded by TextLabel.TextColor3 which should be used in all new work.

kid.simple: Old — use TextColor3 instead.

m.d: This property determines the color of all the text rendered by the TextLabel element.
m.s: Determines the color of rendered text.

kid.simple: The color of the text.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255) -- white text

m.d:
This property sets the base direction in which the TextLabel orders and renders its text, using a value of the TextDirection enum. It defaults to TextDirection.Auto, which infers the direction from the content of Text so that left-to-right and right-to-left scripts are ordered correctly. Set it to TextDirection.LeftToRight or TextDirection.RightToLeft to force a specific direction regardless of the text content.

This property supports styling.
m.s: Direction in which the text is rendered.

kid.simple: Which way the text reads. Auto (default) figures it out from the language, so languages like Arabic read right-to-left. You can force LeftToRight or RightToLeft.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextDirection = Enum.TextDirection.Auto

m.d: This read-only property is true when the text rendered by the TextLabel fits entirely within the element's GuiBase2d.AbsoluteSize, and false when the text is too large and is therefore clipped or truncated. It's computed from TextBounds relative to the available space, so it reflects the combined effect of TextWrapped, TextTruncate, and TextScaled.
m.s: A boolean representation of whether the label's text fits within the size of it.

kid.simple: Read-only. true if all the text fits inside, false if some of it is cut off.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
if not label.TextFits then
	print("Text is too long for this box!")
end

m.d:
This property determines whether text is scaled so that it fills the label's entire space. When enabled, TextSize is ignored and TextWrapped is automatically enabled. This property is useful for rendering text elements within BillboardGuis. When this property is used for on-screen UI, it may be helpful to use a UITextSizeConstraint to restrict the range of possible text sizes.

Automatic Sizing

It's recommended that you avoid usage of TextScaled and adjust UI to take advantage of the AutomaticSize property instead. Here are the core differences between the two properties:

  • TextScaled scales the content (text) to accommodate the UI. Without careful consideration, some text may become unreadable if scaled too small.

  • AutomaticSize resizes the UI to accommodate content while maintaining a consistent font size. For more information, see here.

Additionally, it's recommended that you avoid applying both AutomaticSize and TextScaled and to the same TextLabel. AutomaticSize determines the maximum amount of available space that a GuiObject can use (in this case, text), while TextScaled uses the available space determined by AutomaticSize to scale the font size up to the maximum font size (100) if there are no size constraints.
m.s: Changes whether text is resized to fit within the `Class.TextLabel`.

kid.simple: When true, the text automatically grows or shrinks to fill the whole box (TextSize is ignored and wrapping turns on). Great for BillboardGuis and SurfaceGuis.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextScaled = true
kid.gotcha: Text can become tiny and hard to read. Add a UITextSizeConstraint to set a min/max size, and don't combine it with AutomaticSize.

m.d: This property determines the height of one line of rendered text. The unit is in offsets, not points (which is used in most document editing programs). The Font.Legacy font does not hold this property.
m.s: Determines the line height of text in offsets.

kid.simple: How tall one line of text is, in pixels. 14 is small, 24 is medium, 48 is big. Ignored when TextScaled is on.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextSize = 24
kid.gotcha: Try not to go below 9; tiny text is hard to read for many players.

m.d:
This property sets the color of the stroke, or outline, of rendered text. Along with TextStrokeTransparency, it determines the final visual appearance of the text stroke.

As a powerful alternative which supports color gradients, see UIStroke.
m.s: Determines the color of the text stroke (outline).

kid.simple: The color of the outline drawn around each letter. Only shows when TextStrokeTransparency is less than 1.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextStrokeColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0) -- black outline
label.TextStrokeTransparency = 0             -- make it visible
kid.gotcha: For thicker or gradient outlines, use a UIStroke instead.

m.d:
This property sets the transparency of the stroke, or outline, of rendered text. Along with TextStrokeColor3, it determines the final visual appearance of the text stroke.

Note that text stroke is multiple renderings of the same transparency, so this property is essentially multiplicative on itself four times over. Therefore, it's recommended to set TextStrokeTransparency to a value in the range of 0.75 to 1 for more a more subtle effect.

As a powerful alternative which supports color gradients, see UIStroke.
m.s: Determines the transparency of the text stroke (outline).

kid.simple: How see-through the letter outline is. 1 (default) = no outline, 0 = solid outline. The outline is drawn several times stacked, so even 0.5 looks quite solid; 0.75 to 1 gives a soft outline.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextStrokeTransparency = 0.5

m.d: This property determines the transparency of all the text rendered by the TextLabel.
m.s: Determines the transparency of rendered text.

kid.simple: How see-through the text is. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible. Doesn't affect the background box (that's BackgroundTransparency).
kid.example:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local label = script.Parent
-- Fade the text out over 1 second
TweenService:Create(label, TweenInfo.new(1), {TextTransparency = 1}):Play()

m.d:
This property controls how the TextLabel truncates text that is too large to fit within the element, using a value of the TextTruncate enum. It defaults to TextTruncate.None, which leaves text untruncated. TextTruncate.AtEnd truncates at word boundary and replaces the overflowing graphemes with an ellipsis (...), respecting word boundaries where possible, while TextTruncate.SplitWord truncates inside a word when the line ends in the middle of one.

This property supports styling.
m.s: Controls the truncation of the text displayed in the `Class.TextLabel`.

kid.simple: What to do with text that's too long to fit. None (default) just cuts it off. AtEnd replaces the end with "...". SplitWord can cut in the middle of a word.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd -- "A really long na..."

m.d: This property determines whether or not text should wrap at the edges of the TextLabel element's space.
m.s: Determines whether or not text should wrap at the edges of the `Class.TextLabel` element's space.
m.dep: This property is simply an alias for TextWrapped. Use the past-tense version instead.

kid.simple: Old — use TextWrapped instead.

m.d:
When enabled, this property will render text on multiple lines within a TextLabel element's space so that TextBounds will never exceed the GuiBase2d.AbsoluteSize of the element. This is achieved by breaking long lines of text into multiple lines.

Line breaks will prefer whitespace; should a long unbroken word exceed the width of the element, that word will be broken into multiple lines.

If further line breaks would cause the vertical height of the text (the Y component of TextBounds) to exceed the vertical height of the element (the Y component of GuiBase2d.AbsoluteSize), then that line will not be rendered at all.
m.s: Determines if text wraps to multiple lines within the `Class.TextLabel`

kid.simple: When true, long text continues on the next line instead of running off the side. It prefers to break at spaces. Lines that don't fit vertically aren't shown.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextWrapped = true

m.d:
This property determines the horizontal alignment of text rendered within the object's space. It is used in conjunction with TextYAlignment to fully determine text alignment on both axes.

Note that this property won't affect the read-only properties TextBounds and TextFits.
m.s: Determines the horizontal alignment of rendered text.

kid.simple: Lines the text up sideways inside the box: Left, Center (default) or Right.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left

m.d:
This property determines the vertical alignment of text rendered within the object's space. It is used in conjunction with TextXAlignment to fully determine text alignment on both axes.

Note that this property won't affect the read-only properties TextBounds and TextFits.
m.s: Determines the vertical alignment of rendered text.

kid.simple: Lines the text up up-and-down inside the box: Top, Center (default) or Bottom.
kid.example:
local label = script.Parent
label.TextYAlignment = Enum.TextYAlignment.Top

kid.simple: A TextLabel is a box that shows text. Use it for titles, scores, timers, names and messages. You can change the words, the font, the color, the size, and whether the background box shows at all.
kid.analogy: A TextLabel is like a name sticker: a piece of paper (the background) with words written on it. You can even peel off the paper and keep only the words by making the background invisible.
whenToUse: Showing a score, coin count, or timer
Titles and headings in menus
Messages like 'Round starting in 5...'
Names above heads (inside a BillboardGui)
kid.where: Inside a ScreenGui, SurfaceGui or BillboardGui. Create it in Studio or with Instance.new("TextLabel") in a LocalScript (for one player's screen) or a Script (for a SurfaceGui/BillboardGui everyone sees in Workspace).

terms.UI / GUI: User Interface: the buttons, menus, text and pictures drawn on the screen or on things in the game.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. All UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.ScreenGui: The invisible container that holds UI shown on the player's screen. It must be inside the player's PlayerGui (put it in StarterGui in Studio).
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside.
terms.UDim2: The value used for Size and Position: (X Scale, X Offset, Y Scale, Y Offset). Scale is a fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size; Offset is exact pixels.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.transparency: How see-through something is. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible.
terms.Color3: A color made of red, green and blue amounts, like Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0) for red.
terms.font: The style of the letters, like Arial, Comic, or a blocky game font.
terms.rich text: Text with simple tags inside it, like word, that make parts bold, italic or colored.
terms.grapheme: One visible character, like a letter, a number, or a symbol.
terms.wrap: When text reaches the edge, it continues on the next line.
terms.truncate: Cut off text that's too long, often adding '...' at the end.
terms.read-only: You can read the value but not change it.
terms.localization: Translating text into the player's language.
terms.deprecated: Old and replaced by something better. Don't use it in new code.

examples.title: A countdown timer in the middle of the screen
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Parent = playerGui

local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
label.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.3) -- centered, 30% down the screen
label.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(400, 80)
label.BackgroundTransparency = 1           -- no box, only text
label.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
label.TextStrokeTransparency = 0           -- black outline so it's readable anywhere
label.TextSize = 48
label.FontFace = Font.fromEnum(Enum.Font.GothamBold)
label.Parent = screenGui

for seconds = 5, 1, -1 do
	label.Text = "Starting in " .. seconds
	task.wait(1)
end
label.Text = "GO!"
task.wait(1)
label.Visible = false
explain: AnchorPoint (0.5, 0.5) and Position X 0.5 put the label's middle in the middle of the screen sideways.
BackgroundTransparency = 1 hides the box so only the white text shows.
TextStrokeTransparency = 0 adds a solid outline so the text is readable on bright or dark backgrounds.
The for loop counts 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, changing Text and waiting 1 second each time.

gotchas: Text cut off? Turn on TextWrapped, make the label bigger, use AutomaticSize, or use TextScaled.
BackgroundTransparency hides the box but not the text. TextTransparency hides the text.
Text a player typed, shown to OTHER players, must be filtered with TextService first, or your game could be moderated.
Use TextColor3, not the old TextColor, and TextWrapped, not the old TextWrap.

class/TextService.d: TextService is internally responsible for handling the display of text.
class/TextService.s: Service internally responsible for handling the display of text.

m.d: This method is no longer supported and should not be used. Translating chat messages is only available via TextChatService.
m.s: Filters and translates a string.
m.dep: This method is no longer supported and should not be used. All calls return an empty object.

m.d:
This method filters a string being received from a user and returns a TextFilterResult which can be used to distribute the correctly filtered text accordingly.

This method should be called once each time a user submits a message. If it fails, do not display the text to any user.

See text filtering for usage guidelines and examples.

Notes

  • This method always yields to make a text filtering service call.
  • This method may throw if there is a service error that cannot be resolved. In such cases, do not retry the request, as this method implements its own retry logic internally.
  • This method currently throws if fromUserId is not online on the current server.
m.s: Filters a string being received from a user and returns a

p.s: The text to be filtered.
The Player.UserId of the player filtering the text.
The context that the filtered message will be used in. This parameter does not impact the filtered result of the query and is only used to improve Roblox's text filtering.

r.s: A TextFilterResult that wraps the filtered text and exposes methods for retrieving it in the form appropriate for each audience.

m.d:
Returns a table containing the name and faces of a font family. If the font family has already been loaded by a previous call to GetFamilyInfoAsync(), ContentProvider:PreloadAsync(), or a text object with the TextLabel.FontFace property set, then the method returns without yielding.

This method can fail because of network errors and should be wrapped in LuaGlobals.pcall() to catch and handle errors.
m.s: Returns a table containing the name and faces of a font family.

p.s: Asset ID of the font family to look up.

r.s: The information about the font family.

m.d:
Computes the Vector2 dimensions (in pixels) that will be taken up with text when using parameters defined in a GetTextBoundsParams object. This method is similar to GetTextSize() but uses the Font object which has access to more fonts than Font.

This method is a useful alternative to the TextBounds property of the TextLabel/TextButton objects, since GetTextBoundsAsync() can calculate the dimensions required by a particular text string in a TextLabel or TextButton before such an object is created or text property set.

This is a yielding method because some fonts may need to be loaded in order to measure them. As a result, it should be wrapped in LuaGlobals.pcall() to catch and handle errors. If the font is already loaded, it will not yield; ContentProvider:PreloadAsync() can be used to make sure a font is loaded.
m.s: Computes the `Datatype.Vector2` dimensions (in pixels) that will be taken up with text when using a `Class.GetTextBoundsParams` object.

p.s: A reference to a GetTextBoundsParams object.

r.s: The size of the text as a Vector2.

m.d:
Computes the Vector2 dimensions (in pixels) that will be taken up with text when using the specified formatting parameters and size constraints.

This method is a useful alternative to the TextBounds property of the TextLabel/TextButton objects, since GetTextSize() can calculate the dimensions required by a particular text string in a TextLabel or TextButton before such an object is created or text property set.

This method is limited to fonts under Font. To access more fonts under Font, use GetTextBoundsAsync() instead.
m.s: Computes the `Datatype.Vector2` dimensions (in pixels) that will be taken up with text when using the specified formatting parameters and size constraints.

p.s: The string for which the text size is to be calculated.
The integer representing the font size used. Does not accept an FontSize value.
The font used.
The GuiBase2d.AbsoluteSize of the text object to be used. Required to compute how the text will wrap.

r.s: The size of the space required, in pixels, by the string with the specified formatting.

m.d:
Returns the offset used to up-scale text based on GuiService.PreferredTextSize, a property which may change through the player's setting in the Roblox or in‑experience Settings menus.

This offset can be used as an additive value to adjust the core height value of a TextLabel or TextButton based on PreferredTextSize.

Note that, currently, the fontSize and font parameters do not affect the outcome and this method returns merely the offset as described above. Also note that this method can fail because of network errors and should be wrapped in LuaGlobals.pcall() to catch and handle errors.
m.s: Returns the offset used to up-scale text based on the current `Class.GuiService.PreferredTextSize` setting.

p.s: The font size, in offsets. This parameter currently does not affect the returned offset.
The font. This parameter currently does not affect the returned offset.

r.s: The offset, in pixels, to add to the height of a TextLabel or TextButton to up-scale it for the player's current PreferredTextSize setting.

class/TextSource.d:
Represents a speaker in a TextChannel.

TextSources provide details on permissions users have in TextChannels. There may be multiple TextSources for a user if that user belongs in multiple TextChannels.

Create TextSources with TextChannel:AddUserAsync(), which adds a TextSource to the TextChannel as a descendant.

Remove TextSources by calling TextSource.Destroy.

Name of a TextSource is the Player.DisplayName of the user associated with the TextSource via TextSource.UserId.

To learn more about using TextSources, see In-Experience Text Chat.

m.d:
Determines whether the user can send messages to the TextChannel.

If false, user can only read messages in the TextChannel.
m.s: Determines whether the user can send messages to the `Class.TextChannel`.

m.d:
UserId of the user represented by the TextSource.

Support for non-user entities may be added in the future via passing in negative numbers for this property.
m.s: UserId of the user represented by the `Class.TextSource`.

class/Texture.d:
A Texture object applies a repeating image texture to the face of a parent BasePart. The affected face is dependent on the Face property. Unlike Decals, the texture applied by a Texture will repeat when the parent BasePart is resized, with the size of the repeating textures determined by the StudsPerTileU and StudsPerTileV properties.

The applied image texture is determined by its ColorMapContent property. For details on how to upload images, see asset management.

For more information, review textures and decals. See also:

  • Decal for non-repeating surface images.
  • MeshPart.TextureContent to apply an image texture to a MeshPart.
  • SurfaceGui to apply an ImageLabel or ImageButton to an in-experience 3D object.
class/Texture.s: Applies a repeating image texture to the face of a parent `Class.BasePart`.

m.d:
This property determines how far the rendered texture is offset on the horizontal axis, in studs, as visualized here.

See also OffsetStudsV.
m.s: Determines the offset in studs of the rendered texture's horizontal coordinate.

m.d:
This property determines how far the rendered texture is offset on the vertical axis, in studs, as visualized here.

See also OffsetStudsU.
m.s: Determines the offset in studs of the rendered texture's vertical coordinate.

m.d:
Sets the horizontal size, in studs, of the tiled image applied by the Texture.

Larger values for this property will lead to the Texture appearing larger, and repeating less frequently. Unlike with Decals, the size of the repeated image is unaffected by the dimensions of the BasePart. Instead, resizing the BasePart only increases the number of times the texture repeats.

Note that this property can be set to very low values, but not zero. Also note that the horizontal/vertical distinction is relative to the parent BasePart axis; therefore the Texture will rotate along with the BasePart.

See also StudsPerTileV.
m.s: Sets the horizontal size, in studs, of the tiled image applied by the `Class.Texture`.

m.d:
Sets the vertical size, in studs, of the tiled image applied by the Texture.

Larger values for this property will lead to the Texture appearing larger, and repeating less frequently. Unlike with Decals, the size of the repeated image is unaffected by the dimensions of the BasePart. Instead, resizing the BasePart only increases the number of times the texture repeats.

Note that this property can be set to very low values, but not zero. Also note that the horizontal/vertical distinction is relative to the parent BasePart axis; therefore the Texture will rotate along with the BasePart.

See also StudsPerTileU.
m.s: Sets the vertical size, in studs, of the tiled image applied by the `Class.Texture`.

class/TimerService.d: An internal service responsible for scheduling timed events. It is used by the Debris class. Its functionality can not be accessed by developers.
class/TimerService.s: An internal service responsible for scheduling timed events. It is used by the `Class.Debris` class. Its functionality can not be accessed by developers.

class/Tool.d: A Tool is an object that a Humanoid object can equip. For players, they are stored in a Backpack object parented to a Player object. In-experience, players may have multiple tools which appear as icons at the bottom of the screen. Equipping a tool moves it from the Backpack and into a Player.Character model in the Workspace. By default, tools are held in the right hand and have a handle in them, which is a BasePart named Handle inside (although one isn't required if Tool.RequiresHandle is false). Tools that are to be provided to (re)spawning players should be stored in the StarterPack.
class/Tool.s: An object, such as a weapon, that can be equipped by a `Class.Humanoid`.

m.d:
The CanBeDropped property controls whether the player can drop the Tool.

If true, when the backspace button is pressed, the tool will be parented to Workspace and removed from the player's Backpack. If false, nothing will happen when backspace is pressed, and the tool will remain equipped.
m.s: Controls whether the player can drop the tool.

kid.simple: If true, the player can drop the tool by pressing Backspace; it falls into Workspace. If false, Backspace does nothing.
kid.example: tool.CanBeDropped = false

m.d:
The Enabled property relates to whether or not the Tool can be used. This is useful if you want to prevent a player from using a tool, but don't want to remove it from their Backpack.

When set to true, the player can use the tool. When set to false, the tool is disabled and the player cannot use it; this prevents the tool from being activated or deactivated by the Tool:Activate() and Tool:Deactivate() methods, and it prevents the Tool.Activated and Tool.Deactivated events from firing.
m.s: Relates to whether or not the tool can be used.

kid.simple: If false, the tool can't be used: Activated and Deactivated won't fire. It stays in the Backpack. Great for cooldowns.
kid.example:
tool.Enabled = false
task.wait(3) -- 3 second cooldown
tool.Enabled = true

m.d: The Grip property stores the tool's "grip" properties as a single CFrame. These properties position how the player holds the tool and include GripUp, GripRight, GripForward, and GripPos.
m.s: Stores the tool's "grip" properties as one `Datatype.CFrame`.

kid.simple: A CFrame that sets where and how the tool sits in the hand, measured from the hand. Change its position to slide the tool in the hand and its rotation to tilt it. You usually tweak it until it looks right.
kid.example: tool.Grip = CFrame.new(0, -1, 0) -- hold the tool 1 stud further along its handle

m.d:
One of the properties that specifies a tool's orientation in a character's hand. This represents the R02, R12, and R22 values of the grip CFrame rotation matrix.

Other tool properties that control how a character holds a tool include Tool.GripUp, Tool.GripRight, and Tool.GripPos. All of these properties are stored in a single CFrame in the Tool.Grip property.
m.s: Represents the `R02`, `R12`, and `R22` values of the grip `Datatype.CFrame` rotation matrix.

kid.simple: Hidden. One piece of the Grip rotation. Just use Tool.Grip.

m.d:
